newsitem.title: FRANCE: France applauds Zaire rebel decision on refugees.
newsitem.headline: France applauds Zaire rebel decision on refugees.

text.p: France on Monday applauded a decision by Zairean rebels to allow an airlift to repatriate up to 100,000 Rwandan refugees but said aid groups must be given free access to eastern Zaire to distribute aid.
"This means that the request of the (United Nations) High Commissioner for Refugees to use the airport at Kisangani has finally been heard," the foreign ministry said.
Tens of thousands of refugees have been stranded in eastern Zaire by the advance of rebels led by Laurent Kabila, seeking to topple Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.

Until Saturday, the rebels had insisted the refugees, camped along a rail track south of Kisangani and reported to be dying at the rate of at least 120 a day, had to be repatriated by roads that are virtually impassible.

But intense international pressure on the rebels over the previous two days apparently forced a change of mind on the same day the rebels sat down in South Africa for their first negotiations with Mobutu's crippled regime.
The Hutus, many emaciated and sick, left their camps in eastern Zaire, close to Rwanda's border six months ago.
France said international aid organisations must now be granted free access to rebel-held territory to hand out aid to the refugees until the airlift is complete.
Some experts estimate that the complicated and hugely expensive operation, expected to start in a few days, could take three months to complete.
"It is indispensible that the transport of humanitarian assistance to all those in need be guaranteed, while the repatriation is completed," the ministry said in a statement.
France also said it hoped the talks in South Africa would lead to a quick ceasefire.
